# Environment variables

Every variable the server reads. Set them on the container; `deploy/deployment.yaml` lists the common ones. **Default** is what the server uses when the variable is unset; the image and `deploy/deployment.yaml` set a few themselves.

## Core

A value that doesn't parse, or is below the minimum, falls back to the default.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port the server listens on (API, UI, `/metrics`, probes). |
| `DATA_PATH` | `./data/app.db`; image: `/data/app.db` | SQLite database file. Must be on a persistent volume; the directory also holds session recordings unless `SESSION_RECORDING_DIR` is set. |
| `STATIC_DIR` | `./public`; image: `/app/public` | Directory of the React build the server serves. |
| `TIMEZONE` | `UTC`; `deployment.yaml`: `Europe/Istanbul` | Time zone of audit log timestamps in the UI and CSV export. |
| `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | How long audit events are kept in the database; older ones are purged automatically. |
| `API_KEY_READ_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | How long **successful reads made with an API key** (`list`, `get`, `logs`, `view_yaml`, `view_overview`) are kept; they are most of an agent's audit volume. Writes, denials, failures, `pod.exec` and `api_key.*` events stay for `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS`. Console / Elastic lines are not affected. |
| `RESTART_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | How long container exits (restart history) are kept. |
| `MAX_REPLICAS` | `100` | Highest replica count the Scale endpoint accepts for Deployments and StatefulSets. |

## Logging

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LOG_FORMAT` | `text`; `deployment.yaml`: `ecs` | `ecs` (Elastic Common Schema, nested JSON; use it for Elastic), `json` (flat JSON with short field names) or `text` (for reading by eye). |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. Successful health probes and `/metrics` scrapes are logged at `debug` only. |
| `LOG_OUTPUT` | `stdout` | `stdout` or `stderr`. |
| `LOG_ADD_SOURCE` | `false` | Add the source file and line to every record (`log.origin.*` in ECS). |
| `LOG_INCLUDE_AUDIT` | `true` | Write every audit event to stdout as well, one line per action, with the request id of its HTTP request line. With `false` the database still has them. |
| `APP_ENV` | none; `deployment.yaml`: `prod` | Environment label on every log record (`service.environment`) and trace (`deployment.environment`), e.g. `prod`. |
| `APP_VERSION` | the build version | Overrides the version on log records and traces (`service.version`), e.g. for a canary. |

## Tracing (OpenTelemetry)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | none | OTLP/HTTP receiver, e.g. `http://otel-collector.observability:4318`. Setting this or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` turns tracing on; the other `OTEL_*` variables of the OpenTelemetry specification (headers, sampler, resource attributes) apply as well. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` | none | OTLP/HTTP endpoint for traces only (full URL, including `/v1/traces`). |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `openconsole` | `service.name` of the traces. |

## Security and limits

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` | `8` | Minimum length of local passwords (create, change, admin reset). Passwords are also capped at 72 bytes (bcrypt). |
| `EXEC_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `5m` | A pod shell with no input for this long is closed. Go duration (`90s`, `10m`, `1h`); minimum `30s`. |
| `MAX_EXEC_SESSIONS_PER_USER` | `3` | Open pod shells per user; one more is refused with 429 and audited as `pod.exec` / `rate_limited`. `0` = unlimited. |

## Sign-in

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_AD_AUTHORITY` | `https://login.microsoftonline.com` | Microsoft Entra ID sign-in host for national clouds, e.g. `https://login.microsoftonline.us` or `https://login.chinacloudapi.cn`. |

## Session recording

Recording is configured in **Admin → Recordings → Recording settings** and stored in the database. These variables only seed those settings on the very first start (useful for scripted installs), except `SESSION_RECORDING_DIR`, which is read on every start.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION_RECORDING_DIR` | `<dir of DATA_PATH>/recordings` | Where `.cast` files are written. Read on every start. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_ENABLED` | `true` | Record new pod shell sessions. Seeds Admin → Recordings on the first start only, like the variables below; after that the setting in the UI wins. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | Daily purge of older recordings; `0` = never. First start only. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_MAX_SIZE_MB` | `10` | Per-session cap; past it the recording stops and is flagged truncated. First start only. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_MAX_TOTAL_MB` | `2048` | Quota for all recordings together. First start only. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_MIN_FREE_MB` | `512` | Free space always left on the recordings volume. First start only. |
| `SESSION_RECORDING_DISK_POLICY` | `evict_oldest` | What happens at the quota: `evict_oldest` deletes the oldest recordings, `stop` stops recording new sessions. First start only. |

## Feature flags

Switch a capability off **for everyone, admins included**, whatever the roles grant: `FEATURE_<NAME>=false` (or `0`, `no`). Anything else, or unset, leaves it on. A disabled feature disappears from the UI, its endpoints answer 403 `feature_disabled` and the attempt is audited as `denied`. `GET /api/features` shows the current state; the startup log lists what is off.

| Variable | `false` turns off |
|---|---|
| `FEATURE_POD_EXEC` | pod shell and one-command exec (`pods:exec`) |
| `FEATURE_YAML_EDIT` | YAML edit / apply on every resource except Secrets (`{resource}:edit`) |
| `FEATURE_WORKLOAD_ACTIONS` | Deployment restart and scale, StatefulSet scale |
| `FEATURE_SECRETS` | the whole Secrets tab (every `secrets:*`) |
| `FEATURE_SECRET_REVEAL` | revealing secret values (`secrets:reveal`) |
| `FEATURE_SECRET_EDIT` | editing Secrets (`secrets:edit`) |
| `FEATURE_API_KEYS` | API keys: the page, the `/api/me/api-keys` endpoints and signing in with a key (a key then gets 401) |
